experiment: SYNK video preflight final comparison on production scripts, 2026-11-03

method.sample: Five purposely selected production videos, eight whole-script pairs. Three SYNK Brief shorts, a five-scene SHIFT clinic and an eighteen-chapter SHIFT class. Separate ASR and subtitle pairs use the same script where available. No length padding or invented edits.
method.metric: Median of three fresh Node process medians; each process takes seven rotating, per-call batch averages after 500 warm-up calls per implementation. Full compareText input handling and output object included; WASM copying and calls included. Prior and final JS and release WASM agreed on all result fields before each timing run.
method.excluded: ASR generation, subtitle parsing, one-time startup and media decoding are outside the warm character comparison. Cold WASM and full CLI wall times are recorded separately. Measurements ran sequentially on one desktop with other loads uncontrolled.
method.inputDetails: B23 and B24 use final speech sheets and local unprompted ASR of the original masters. The studio photo short uses its saved ASR and SRT. SHIFT audio ASR and delivered SRT pair with canonical narration in production order; ASR receipts bind to the same narration and audio hashes. SRT uses the same subtitleInspect and subtitleTranscript functions as the preflight tool.
method.historyScope: Local retained pre-upload media-inspection receipts with complete=true in .tmp/올리기전검사 at inventory time. All inspected receipts supplied video alone and had no comparisons.

wholeCli.method: A new Node CLI process per observation. Two original rendered masters with script and recorded ASR, twelve runs per engine per video. All six engine orders occur exactly twice per video. The first 36 observations did not balance order by title. The next 36 filled the missing orders. All 72 are included. Shipping JS uses the original entry. Frozen JS and Rust use byte-identical isolated entry copies binding only compareTextJs to the alternative. Rust initializes once at startup. Media input, normalization, external binaries, status, issues, frames and comparison output agree within each video. Includes Node startup, disk verification, ffprobe, ffmpeg and writing reports. ASR was prepared separately and file caches were not flushed.
